attribution.note: Marcus states the training facts and his personal impression in his own voice.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves the facility count, training duration, compute comparison and subjective qualification.

contract.note: Reading two data centers as two facilities is ordinary and fair. Excluding the personal impression from grading is appropriate.

evidence.note: This company disclosure identifies Colossus but does not establish the facility count. Its compute comparison uses a different baseline, so it does not contradict 15x Grok 2.
The report describes one repurposed facility expanded in two phases. Construction timelines do not establish months of continuous training.
The secondary summary supports approximately 15x Grok 2's compute. It also describes one expanded facility; aggregate GPU-hours do not establish continuous full-time operation for months.

reviews.rationale: The contract explicitly makes training in a single facility sufficient for contradiction, and e2 describes that arrangement. The 15x component has secondary support, while continuous full-time training for months remains unverified. The subjective impression is not graded.

attribution.note: Marcus endorses his account of the exchange and his qualified fact-checking conclusion.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves his uncertainty about the earthquake and his admission that the prompt may have been too terse.

contract.note: The contract turns a qualified finding into categorical fabrication and assumes the exchange occurred as described. Its search bounds cannot identify the alleged quake without its date or magnitude.

evidence.note: The catalog supports absence of recorded earthquakes within the specified dates, radius and magnitude threshold. It does not establish what Grok said or whether those bounds cover the alleged event.

reviews.rationale: The earthquake conclusion is explicitly qualified and cannot be scored as a firm assertion under this policy. The catalog supports only a bounded absence finding. The firm account of Grok's response remains independently unverified; the contract cannot establish it by accepting Marcus's description.
